decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott + Gholdengo to establish priority Tailwind and immediately pressure rain teams with Make It Rain, while Taunt can deny Tailwind/Wide Guard. Milotic provides strong Water/Ice coverage and Competitive punishment; Tauros adds Intimidate, fast Close Combat, and Rock Slide pressure into Archaludon and Pelipper.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s preview strongly suggests Pelipper rain and Archaludon support, with possible Mega Swampert rain offense. Prioritize denying opposing Tailwind or Wide Guard with Whimsicott, then use Gholdengo spread pressure. Preserve Milotic for Water/Ground threats and Tauros for Archaludon/Pelipper pressure. Watch for Mega Swampert’s Swift Swim and Wide Guard users.

decisions.rationale: Lead Swampert and Pelipper to set immediate Rain and enable Swift Swim alongside Wide Guard to neutralize Gholdengo's Make It Rain and Sinistcha's Matcha Gotcha. Bring Archaludon to abuse instant 1-turn Electro Shot in Rain and Tsareena to wall Milotic while blocking opponent Prankster status moves with Queenly Majesty.
decisions.notebook: Plan: Rain offense with Swampert + Pelipper lead supported by Archaludon and Tsareena. Pelipper Wide Guard shuts down Make It Rain, Matcha Gotcha, and Rock Slide. Swampert Mega Swift Swim outspeeds and heavy-hits Gholdengo and Whimsicott. Archaludon fires 1-turn Electro Shot in Rain and gains Stamina boosts. Tsareena blocks Prankster Taunt/Encore/Parting Shot with Queenly Majesty and threatens Milotic with Power Whip.

decisions.rationale: Set Tailwind immediately with Prankster, ensuring Gholdengo remains ahead even if Swampert Mega Evolves under rain. Thunderbolt then acts before Pelipper and guarantees its OHKO, preventing Tailwind or Wide Guard from taking effect.
decisions.notebook: Against rain leads, prioritize immediate speed control while using Gholdengo's single-target Thunderbolt to remove Pelipper before it can establish Tailwind or Wide Guard. Preserve Milotic for Water/Ground pressure and Tauros for Steel/Dragon and Flying targets. Track Mega Swampert's Swift Swim speed and deny Wide Guard when spread attacks are required.

decisions.rationale: Keep Whimsicott in to retain Tailwind speed control and Prankster utility. Bring in Milotic to pressure Mega Swampert and punish any further Water/Ground-focused play; preserve Tauros for later Steel/Dragon or Flying targets.
decisions.notebook: Against rain teams, establish Tailwind and remove Pelipper before it can use Tailwind or Wide Guard. selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Swampert)
decisions.rationale: Mega Swampert in Rain with Swift Swim outspeeds Gholdengo (unless boosted by Whimsicott's Prankster Tailwind with high Speed investment) and threatens a heavy OHKO or massive damage with 2x super-effective High Horsepower. Pelipper's priority +3 Wide Guard completely blocks Gholdengo's main threat, Make It Rain, protecting both active allies on turn 1.
decisions.notebook: G1 Turn 1: Lead Swampert + Pelipper vs Whimsicott + Gholdengo. Rain active (8 turns). Plan: Wide Guard to block Make It Rain while Mega Swampert attacks Gholdengo with High Horsepower.

decisions.rationale: Bringing in Archaludon to capitalize on the 7 turns of Rain remaining. Archaludon's Electro Shot triggers instantly in Rain for free +1 SpA boosts, and its Steel/Dragon typing resists Grass and Water while threatening Whimsicott with Flash Cannon and Milotic with Electro Shot.

Pelipper Wide Guarded but took Thunderbolt from Gholdengo and fainted. Whimsicott set Tailwind (4 turns left). Rain active (7 turns left). Foe back: Milotic, Sinistcha, Grimmsnarl, Tauros.

decisions.rationale: Encore locks Swampert-Mega into its revealed High Horsepower, preventing Ice Punch or Protect while Tailwind preserves speed control. Milotic uses Ice Beam on Archaludon for direct neutral damage instead of Muddy Water into its Water resistance.

decisions.rationale: In Rain, Electro Shot charges instantly and grants Archaludon +1 Special Attack before attacking. Combined with Swampert's High Horsepower into Milotic, we deal 91.1-195.9% total damage, creating a near-guaranteed KO on Milotic unless it Protects. Choosing High Horsepower now also neutralizes Whimsicott's Prankster Encore threat, as being locked into High Horsepower remains productive while avoiding Protect-lock traps.

Whimsicott set Tailwind. Rain active. Brought Archaludon. Foe back: Milotic + 1 of (Sinistcha, Grimmsnarl, Tauros).

decisions.rationale: Taunt Archaludon to invalidate its Encore-locked Electro Shot if Close Combat misses the KO, while Tauros attacks it with super-effective Close Combat. This pressures the most dangerous boosted foe and leaves Swampert stuck using its weaker Encore-locked High Horsepower.
decisions.notebook: Against rain teams, establish Tailwind and remove Pelipper before it can use Tailwind or Wide Guard. Preserve Tauros for Steel/Dragon and Flying targets. Encore can lock dangerous foes into poor attacks; Taunt can then invalidate an Encore-locked move.

decisions.rationale: Both active Pokémon are locked into their moves via Encore. Tauros is the primary offensive threat with Expert Belt Close Combat, which Archaludon easily survives at full HP (36.5-67% max damage) while triggering Stamina (+1 Def). Combining Swampert's High Horsepower (30-55%) and Archaludon's +2 SpA Rain-boosted Electro Shot (85-165%) into Tauros guarantees a KO unless Tauros Protects. If Tauros Protects, opponent's Tailwind expires at turn end, allowing Swampert to outspeed next turn.
decisions.notebook: G1 T1: Whimsicott + Gholdengo lead. Swampert Mega Evolved, KO'd Gholdengo with High Horsepower. Pelipper fainted to Gholdengo Thunderbolt. Rain up (Damp Rock). Foe back: Milotic, Tauros. G2 Plan: Swampert + Archaludon strong core in Rain.

decisions.rationale: Encore Swampert into High Horsepower, which is resisted by Whimsicott, while Archaludon remains locked into Electro Shot and cannot use Protect under Taunt. This maximizes Whimsicott's chance to survive and preserve control.
decisions.notebook: Against rain teams, prioritize removing weather-setting support early and preserve answers to Steel/Dragon threats. Encore opposing attackers into resisted or ineffective moves whenever possible; use Taunt to prevent defensive recovery or disruptive options after establishing a lock.

decisions.rationale: Swampert outspeeds Whimsicott in Rain (224 vs max 184) and hits first with 100% accurate Ice Punch to deal chunk damage/pop Sash. Archaludon follows up with +3 SpA Electro Shot into Whimsicott for the double target finish and Game 1 victory.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 won 1-0. Core strategy with Mega Swampert and Archaludon in Rain overwhelmed Whimsicott/Gholdengo/Milotic/Tauros. Foe brought Whimsicott (FocusSash: Tailwind, Taunt, Encore, Moonblast), Gholdengo (LifeOrb), Milotic (Leftovers), Tauros (ExpertBelt). Sinistcha and Grimmsnarl left on bench.

reflections.summary: The loss was primarily a preview/selection mismatch: no Mega was brought or evolved, and this four lacked immediate pressure on rain-boosted Archaludon. Its repeated Electro Shot boosts reached +4 while Mega Swampert stayed healthy; the critical hit on Tauros only accelerated an already losing position.
reflections.adjustment: Change the four for this matchup: replace the least useful rain matchup slot, preferably Milotic, with a Mega Stone holder that can immediately pressure Archaludon or Swampert, and Mega Evolve it. Pair that pressure with Whimsicott’s Tailwind or Taunt rather than spending turns Encore-locking targets that can continue attacking.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s rain mode uses Damp Rock Pelipper to enable Mega Swampert and rapidly boost Archaludon through Electro Shot. Archaludon has Stamina and can snowball Special Attack while remaining difficult to remove physically; prioritize stopping it before boosts accumulate. Pelipper has Wide Guard, so do not rely solely on spread attacks. Mega Swampert can repeatedly use High Horsepower and remains dangerous even when Encore-locked. Future plan: bring immediate Mega pressure into Archaludon/Swampert, disrupt rain or Electro Shot early, and preserve a dedicated answer to the Steel/Dragon threat.

reflections.summary: Bringing Mega Swampert and Archaludon alongside Pelipper rain support was the optimal team-preview plan; Archaludon's Stamina and Electro Shot boosts easily out-scaled opponent's offense despite Whimsicott's Prankster Encore locks.
reflections.adjustment: Lead or switch in Tsareena early when Whimsicott is on field to shut down Prankster Encore and Taunt with Queenly Majesty.

Left on bench: Sinistcha, Grimmsnarl. Strategic fact: Tsareena's Queenly Majesty invalidates Whimsicott's Prankster disruption.
